main.claim: Paste or type your text into the box and the counts update as you type: words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs and reading time. It runs in your browser, so there is nothing to install.

sections.heading: How to count the words in your text
sections.body:
Open the [word counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/) and click into the box. Paste a draft from a document, an email or a chat, or type straight into the box. The counts start at once and keep updating as you change the text, so you can see the effect of every edit.

1. Open [Word Counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/).
2. Paste or type your text into the box.
3. Read the counts for words, characters, sentences and paragraphs.
4. Edit the text and check the numbers again.

**The counts update as you type.** You do not need to press a button to see the new total.

Words are the groups of letters or numbers that sit between spaces. The word count is useful when a brief, an assignment or a page asks for a length in words.

sections.heading: What each count means
sections.body:
Characters with spaces count every letter, number, punctuation mark and space. Characters without spaces leave the spaces out, so that number is always the lower of the two. Use the first number when a limit counts spaces, and the second when it does not.

Many forms and posting tools count characters, not words, so check which one the limit uses before you trim your text. The same paragraph can fit one limit and fail another.

Sentences and paragraphs are counted too. If the word count is high but the sentence count is low, your sentences are long. Split a few of them and check the count again.

sections.heading: Reading and speaking time
sections.body:
The counter estimates how long your text takes to read and to say out loud. Reading time uses 238 words per minute. Speaking time uses 130 words per minute.

These are fixed rates, so a slow reader, or a speaker who pauses often, will take longer than the number shows. Use speaking time to plan a talk or a video script. A script of 1,300 words comes to about 10 minutes at 130 words per minute.

sections.heading: Limits for posts and forms
sections.body:
The counter has limits built in for four common places. A tweet is limited to 280 characters, an SMS to 160, a meta description to 160 and a LinkedIn post to 3000. Paste the text you plan to post and edit until the count fits.

Platforms can change their limits, so check the platform's own help if a number does not match what you see. The counter is a check on your text, not a promise about how the platform will show it.

sections.heading: Most used words
sections.body: The counter lists the words you use most, so repeats stand out. If the same word appears again and again, swap a few of them for other words or cut the ones that add nothing. The list is a quick way to spot repeats in a long draft, and you decide which changes to make.

sections.heading: Write by voice on your Mac
sections.body: If you write a lot on your Mac, Lazur works in any app there. Hold two keys, talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

pages.title: Word Counter Google: Count Words in Google Docs | Lazur
pages.description: Count words in Google Docs with Tools, then Word count. Or paste any text into Lazur's Word Counter for live words, characters, sentences and paragraphs.
pages.claim: Open your document in Google Docs on your computer, click Tools, then Word count to see the words, characters and pages. For text outside Docs, paste it into Word Counter for live counts as you type.

sections.heading: Count words in Google Docs
sections.body:
Google Docs has a word count window built in. These are the steps from Google's help article.

1. Open a document in Google Docs on your computer.
2. At the top of the page, click Tools, then click Word count.
3. Read the window, which shows the count of words, characters and pages.
4. Click Done to close the window.

Google's help article says headers, footers and footnotes are left out of the count unless you select a section of the document first. If you need the count for part of a document, select that part and check the number again.

sections.heading: Get a live count while you type
sections.body:
Google's help article also describes a setting called Display word count while typing. When it is on, click the Word count box in the bottom left of the page to see Pages, Words, Characters and Characters without spaces.

The help article is [Count the words in a document](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/39003?hl=en). Follow its steps to turn the setting on, because the menu it uses can change as Google updates Docs.

sections.heading: When to use Word Counter instead
sections.body:
Google Docs counts what is inside the document. Word Counter is for text that lives somewhere else: a draft in an email, a post you are writing for a social app, a text message, or a document you have not opened in Docs yet.

Copy the text, then paste it into [Word Counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/google). The counts show words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs and reading time. The counter also has limits for a tweet at 280 characters, an SMS at 160, a meta description at 160 and a LinkedIn post at 3000, so you can check a post before you publish it.

sections.heading: Why two counts can differ
sections.body:
Two counters rarely match to the last word, because they may handle a dash, a number or a line break in a different way. Counting the same text in both places shows you whether the difference matters for your work.

If one number is needed for a school, a client or a limit, use the count from the place where that number will be checked. Copy only the body text you need, paste it into Word Counter, and compare the two numbers.

sections.heading: Copy and paste from Google Docs
sections.body:
To copy text from Docs, select it and press Ctrl+C on Windows or Cmd+C on a Mac. Click into the box in Word Counter and press Ctrl+V or Cmd+V to paste. The counts start as soon as the text is in the box.

Lazur is a Mac app for writing by voice: hold two keys and speak, and it types into the app you are in, Google Docs included, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.q: How do I count words in Google Docs?
faq.a: Open the document on your computer, click Tools at the top of the page, then click Word count. The window shows the count of words, characters and pages. Click Done to close it.

faq.q: How do I turn on word count in Google Docs?
faq.a: Click Tools at the top of the page, then click Word count to see the count. For a live count while you type, Google's help article describes a Display word count while typing setting, and it shows how to turn it on.

faq.q: Why does my Google Docs word count not match Word Counter?
faq.a: The two tools can give different numbers, and Google Docs leaves out headers, footers and footnotes unless you select a section first. Copy only the body text you need, paste it into Word Counter, and compare the two numbers.

pages.title: Word Counter With Spaces: Characters With and Without | Lazur
pages.description: Count characters with spaces and without spaces in one live counter. Paste your text, read both totals, and check limits for posts and forms.
pages.claim: Word Counter shows characters with spaces and characters without spaces. Paste your text and both totals update as you type, along with the word, sentence and paragraph counts.

sections.heading: How to count characters with spaces
sections.body:
Open the [spaces counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/spaces) and paste or type your text into the box.

1. Open [Word Counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/spaces).
2. Paste or type your text into the box.
3. Read the characters with spaces total.
4. Read the characters without spaces total.

Characters with spaces count every character you typed, and each space counts as one. Characters without spaces leave the spaces out, so that number is the lower of the two. Pick the count that matches the limit or the form you are checking.

sections.heading: Check whether a limit counts spaces
sections.body:
Limits are set in characters, and not every limit treats spaces the same way. Before you trim a text, check whether the limit you face counts spaces. A form's help text or a platform's help page usually says so.

Word Counter lists limits for a tweet at 280 characters, an SMS at 160, a meta description at 160 and a LinkedIn post at 3000. Paste the text you plan to post and edit until the count fits the limit you need.

**Count the characters for the limit you face, not the number you remember.** A text that fits one place can run over in another.

sections.heading: Check the same text in Pages on Mac
sections.body:
If you write in Pages on your Mac, the counter there can show characters with spaces and characters without spaces too. Click the View menu button in the toolbar, then choose Show Word Count. The counter appears at the bottom of the page, and you can drag it anywhere on the page.

Click the arrows on the right side of the counter to choose which statistic it shows. Apple's guide is [Show word count and other statistics in Pages on Mac](https://support.apple.com/guide/pages/show-word-count-and-other-statistics-tand47165437/mac).

sections.heading: What the other counts tell you
sections.body:
Word Counter also counts words, sentences and paragraphs, so you can see the shape of the text as well as its length. A high word count with a low sentence count usually means long sentences, which are harder to follow. Break one or two of them up, then check the count again.

The counter estimates reading time at 238 words per minute and speaking time at 130 words per minute. These rates are fixed, so use them as a guide for how long the text takes, not as an exact measure.

sections.heading: Write by voice on your Mac
sections.body: Lazur is a Mac app for writing by voice, so a text can start as speech: hold two keys, talk, and it types into the app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.q: How do I count characters with spaces?
faq.a: Paste your text into Word Counter. It shows characters with spaces and characters without spaces, and both numbers update as you type. Use the first number for a limit that counts spaces.
No. A word count counts words, not spaces, so the spaces do not add to it. Character counts are different: the count with spaces includes every space, and the count without spaces leaves them out.

faq.q: How do I count characters without spaces?
faq.a: Read the characters without spaces total in Word Counter. Paste the text, and the total updates as you type. It is lower than the count with spaces, because the spaces are left out.

pages.title: Word Counter on Mac: Pages, Google Docs and Browser | Lazur
pages.description: Show the word count in Pages on Mac, or count any text in your browser with Lazur's Word Counter. Words, characters, sentences and reading time.
pages.claim: On a Mac, open Pages, click the View menu button, then choose Show Word Count. For text from anywhere else, paste it into Word Counter in your browser to see words, characters, sentences and reading time.

sections.heading: Show the word count in Pages
sections.body:
Pages on Mac has a counter you can keep on the page while you write. These are the steps from Apple's help guide.

1. Open the document in Pages on your Mac.
2. Click the View menu button in the toolbar.
3. Choose Show Word Count. The counter appears at the bottom of the page.
4. Click the arrows on the right side of the counter to change what it shows.

The counter can show characters with spaces, characters without spaces, words, paragraphs and pages. Select some text and the counter shows only that selection. To hide it, click the View menu button again. The menu item may show the name of the statistic it is showing instead, so look for that name.

sections.heading: Count any text in your browser
sections.body:
Word Counter runs in your browser, so you can use it on a Mac with text from a note, an email or a web page. Open [Word Counter](https://word-counter.lazur.app/mac), paste your text into the box, and read the counts. They update as you type.

The counts include words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs and reading time. Reading time uses 238 words per minute, and speaking time uses 130.

The counter reads whatever is in the box, so paste the whole text you want to measure, not a part of it. If you copy from a document with headings, the headings go into the count too. Read the total once you have the full text in place, then edit and read it again.

sections.heading: Count in Google Docs on a Mac
sections.body:
Google Docs on your computer uses the same steps on a Mac. Open the document, click Tools at the top of the page, then click Word count. Read the count of words, characters and pages, then click Done.

Google's help article is [Count the words in a document](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/39003?hl=en). It also says headers, footers and footnotes are left out unless you select a section first.

sections.heading: Check a post before you publish
sections.body:
Word Counter has limits for posts and forms: a tweet at 280 characters, an SMS at 160, a meta description at 160 and a LinkedIn post at 3000. Paste the draft into the counter on your Mac and read the count against the limit before you copy it to the platform.

If the draft is over, cut the least useful sentence first, then check the count again. Keep the final version in the same place you will post from, so you do not paste an old copy by mistake.

sections.heading: Write by voice in any Mac app
sections.body: Lazur is a Mac app for writing by voice: hold two keys and speak, and it types into the app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

faq.q: Where is word count on Mac?
faq.a: In Pages, click the View menu button in the toolbar, then choose Show Word Count. The counter appears at the bottom of the page. In Google Docs, click Tools at the top of the page, then click Word count.

faq.q: How do I hide word count in Pages?
faq.a: Click the View menu button, then choose Hide Word Count. The menu item may show the name of the statistic it is showing instead, so look for that name in the menu. You can drag the counter anywhere on the page while it is on.

faq.q: Is there a word counter for Mac that works in a browser?
faq.a: Yes. Open Word Counter in your browser on your Mac, paste or type your text, and read the live counts. It shows words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs and reading time.
